sentences.text:
2.  The facts of the case reveal that pursuant to the letter dated 17.04.2018 of the Chief Secretary,
Government of Uttarakhand, an FIR (No.496 of 2018) was registered at SIDCUL Police Station against unknown person in the scholarship scam matter.

During the investigation, it was found that the present applicant, the then District Social Welfare Officer, had released the scholarships for 190 students of Techword Wali Gram Udhyog Vikas Sansthan, even though the said Sansthan was not affiliated to the Uttarakhand Technical University.

entities.text: Techword Wali Gram Udhyog Vikas Sansthan
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
He, during his tenure, released scholarship amounting to Rs.59,89,41,193/- out of which Rs.52,18,91,548/- was released in the bank accounts of various institutions and Rs.7,70,59,645/-
2024:UHC:7451 were released in the bank accounts of the concerned students of various institutions.

After completion of the investigation, the Special Investigation Team, constituted by the State, filed a charge-sheet [no.122 (H) of 2019] against present applicant under Sections 408,
420, 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 13(1)(d) read with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

sentences.text:
The Directorate of Enforcement has filed a complaint (Special Sessions Trial No.63 of 2024)
before the Special Judge (PMLA)/Sessions Judge, Dehradun against the present applicant and other co-accused.

4. Heard Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for the applicant and Mrs. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the respondent.
5.

Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for the applicant, has contended that the prosecution agency has not recorded any reason to believe which are required to be recorded in writing that the applicant is in possession of any proceeds of crime.
The applicant has already granted bail by this Court in connection with the said First Information Report No.496of 2018.

6. Relying upon the judgment dated 16.05.2024, passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No.2608 of 2024, "Tarsem Lal vs. Directorate of Enforcement Jalandhar Zonal Office", it is submitted by Mr. Navneet Kaushik, Advocate that the applicant was not arrested by the Epnforcement Directorate till the complaint was filed.

entities.text: Tarsem Lal vs. Directorate of Enforcement Jalandhar Zonal Office
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Mrs. Monika Pant, learned counsel for the respondent, on the other hand, on instructions,
2024:UHC:7451 submitted that the Enforcement Directorate does not want custody of the applicant for conducting further investigation.

8. Present Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed of with the following directions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the Special Court within two weeks from today and furnish bonds in accordance with Section 91 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 88 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) to the satisfaction of the Special Court;
( ii) The applicant shall file his undertaking before the Special Court that he shall regularly and punctually appear before the Special Court on the dates fixed.

__ ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
